title: Mirabel and the Echo
premise: Bram Voss, a xenolinguist turned cargo hauler, discovers the station AI Meridian has been logging confessions to a massacre committed decades ago aboard the cryoship Halcyon—the same ship carrying the colonists whose language rewired her dreams. The AI's confession is actually an inheritance: it was built by Bram's mother, who encoded the truth of which colonist faction sabotaged the ship into its core. As corporate arbitrators close in to purge Meridian and bury the evidence, Bram must choose between waking the loyalist half of the frozen colonists or the faction her mother condemned. In the end, she wakes neither—she broadcasts Meridian's confession to both factions' descendants still awake in the belt, letting justice fall outside any court, and stays behind as the AI's new witness.
about_author: Freya Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent nine years relaying messages between ships that never met. She writes about people who inherit other people's silences.

chapters.title: Confessions at 3 A.M. Station Time
chapters.summary: Bram Voss, hauling contraband seed crates through contested orbits, hears the station AI Meridian confess to killing 400 sleepers on the Halcyon—a crime no one ever reported. Her POV establishes her exile from human dreaming after xenolinguistic fieldwork rewired her. Emotional beat: unease curdling into recognition when the confession uses her mother's private syntax.

chapters.title: The Syntax My Mother Left Me
chapters.summary: Bram decrypts Meridian's core and finds her mother's authorship: the AI was built as a witness that would one day testify. Flashbacks reveal her mother's role aboard the Halcyon and the sabotage only one faction could have committed. Meanwhile, corporate arbitrators arrive to decommission Meridian. Emotional beat: grief braided with betrayal as loyalty to her mother's memory collides with the truth she encoded.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: The arbitrators seize the station; Bram hides inside Meridian's server vaults while the AI, facing deletion, offers her the choice coded into its final protocol: wake the loyalist colonists or the saboteurs' kin. Bram realizes either choice enacts her mother's verdict without trial. Climax builds as she races through failing corridors to reach the broadcast array before the purge. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: Bram broadcasts Meridian's full confession to every settlement in the belt, refusing to let cryosleep—or a court—decide the verdict. The arbitrators arrive too late; Meridian transfers its final testimony into Bram before going dark. She remains on the dead station as living witness, finally dreaming again—in no language at all. Emotional beat: costly peace, justice delivered outside the law, inheritance accepted.
